items.title: 90-Minute Screen-Free Zone
items.description: Turn off all screens 90 minutes before bed. Blue light suppresses melatonin production. Read, journal, or do gentle stretching instead.

items.title: Warm Bath or Shower
items.description: Take a warm bath 1-2 hours before bed. The drop in body temperature afterward signals to your brain it's time to sleep.

items.title: Dim Lights Gradually
items.description: Start dimming household lights 2 hours before bed. Use warm-toned bulbs or candles to signal sunset to your circadian rhythm.

items.title: Sleepy Time Tea Ritual
items.description: Brew chamomile, valerian root, or lavender tea 1 hour before bed. The ritual itself signals wind-down time.

items.title: Worry Journal Dump
items.description: Spend 10 minutes writing down worries and tomorrow's to-dos. Getting thoughts out of your head reduces racing mind at bedtime.

items.title: Cool Room Temperature
items.description: Set bedroom to 65-68°F (18-20°C). Cool temperatures help trigger the natural drop in body temp needed for sleep.

items.title: Blackout Curtains
items.description: Install blackout curtains or use a sleep mask. Complete darkness optimizes melatonin production throughout the night.

items.title: White Noise Machine
items.description: Use white, pink, or brown noise to mask disruptive sounds. Consistent sound helps the brain tune out disturbances.

items.title: Lavender Pillow Spray
items.description: Spritz lavender essential oil spray on pillows. Lavender has been shown to decrease heart rate and blood pressure.

items.title: Declutter Bedroom
items.description: Keep bedroom tidy and free of work materials. A clutter-free space reduces mental stimulation and anxiety.

items.title: Weighted Blanket
items.description: Use a weighted blanket (8-12% of body weight). Deep pressure stimulation can increase serotonin and melatonin.

items.title: Mattress Refresh
items.description: Rotate mattress seasonally, replace every 7-10 years. A supportive mattress reduces pain and improves sleep quality.

items.title: Pillow Stack Check
items.description: Ensure proper neck alignment with the right pillow height. Side sleepers need thicker, back sleepers thinner pillows.

items.title: Remove Electronics
items.description: Keep phones and tablets outside the bedroom or face-down. LED lights can disrupt sleep even through closed eyelids.

items.title: Bedroom for Sleep Only
items.description: Avoid working, watching TV, or eating in bed. Train your brain to associate the bed exclusively with sleep.

items.title: 4-7-8 Breathing
items.description: Inhale 4 seconds, hold 7 seconds, exhale 8 seconds. This activates the parasympathetic nervous system.

items.title: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
items.description: Tense and release each muscle group from toes to head. Takes 10-15 minutes and deeply relaxes the body.

items.title: Body Scan Meditation
items.description: Slowly move attention from head to toe, noticing sensations without judgment. Promotes body awareness and calm.

items.title: Yoga Nidra
items.description: Guided 'yogic sleep' meditation. Lie still while a recording guides you through deep relaxation states.

items.title: Visualization Journey
items.description: Imagine a peaceful place in detail - sounds, smells, textures. This redirects the brain from worries.

items.title: Sleep Stories
items.description: Listen to calm, monotone bedtime stories designed for adults. Apps like Calm and Headspace offer many options.

items.title: ASMR for Sleep
items.description: Find ASMR triggers that relax you - whispers, tapping, brushing sounds. Many find these deeply sleep-inducing.

items.title: Humming Bee Breath
items.description: Close ears, inhale deeply, exhale with humming sound. The vibration calms the nervous system.

items.title: Legs Up the Wall
items.description: Lie with legs vertical against wall for 5-10 minutes. Promotes circulation and calms the nervous system.

items.title: Self-Massage
items.description: Gently massage temples, jaw, neck, and shoulders. Release tension held from the day.

items.title: Consistent Wake Time
items.description: Wake at the same time every day, even weekends. This is the most important factor for sleep regulation.

items.title: Morning Light Exposure
items.description: Get 10-30 minutes of bright light within 1 hour of waking. This sets your circadian clock for the day.

items.title: No Naps After 3pm
items.description: If you nap, keep it before 3pm and under 20 minutes. Late naps steal from nighttime sleep pressure.

items.title: Sleep Window Method
items.description: Calculate your ideal sleep window (usually 7-9 hours) and stick to it. Quality over quantity.

items.title: Gradual Bedtime Shift
items.description: Shift bedtime by 15 minutes every few days. Gradual changes are more sustainable than dramatic ones.

items.title: Tryptophan-Rich Dinner
items.description: Include turkey, eggs, cheese, nuts, or seeds at dinner. Tryptophan is a precursor to melatonin.

items.title: Limit Caffeine After 2pm
items.description: Caffeine has a 6-8 hour half-life. Afternoon coffee can still be in your system at bedtime.

items.title: Avoid Heavy Late Meals
items.description: Finish eating 2-3 hours before bed. Digestion can interfere with sleep quality.

items.title: Magnesium-Rich Snack
items.description: Try banana, almonds, or pumpkin seeds before bed. Magnesium supports muscle relaxation and GABA production.

items.title: Tart Cherry Juice
items.description: Drink 8oz tart cherry juice 1-2 hours before bed. Natural source of melatonin and anti-inflammatory compounds.

items.title: Limit Alcohol
items.description: Alcohol may help you fall asleep but disrupts REM sleep. Avoid within 3 hours of bedtime.

items.title: Hydration Balance
items.description: Stay hydrated during day but limit fluids 2 hours before bed to reduce nighttime bathroom trips.

items.title: Golden Milk
items.description: Warm milk with turmeric, ginger, and honey. Anti-inflammatory and sleep-promoting traditional remedy.

items.title: Kiwi Before Bed
items.description: Eat 2 kiwis 1 hour before sleep. Studies show improved sleep onset and duration.

items.title: Avoid Spicy Foods
items.description: Spicy foods can cause heartburn and raise body temperature, both disruptive to sleep.

items.title: Morning Exercise
items.description: Exercise in the morning for best sleep benefits. Morning workouts enhance circadian rhythm.

items.title: Finish Workouts Early
items.description: Complete vigorous exercise at least 4-6 hours before bed. Exercise raises body temp and alertness.

items.title: Evening Yoga
items.description: Gentle yoga in the evening promotes relaxation. Focus on forward folds, twists, and restorative poses.

items.title: Daily Movement Minimum
items.description: Aim for at least 30 minutes of movement daily. Regular exercise improves sleep quality over time.

items.title: Evening Walk
items.description: Take a gentle 15-20 minute walk after dinner. Aids digestion and provides light movement.

items.title: Worry Time Earlier
items.description: Schedule 15 minutes of 'worry time' in the afternoon. Write worries down then close the notebook.

items.title: Cognitive Shuffle
items.description: Think of random unconnected images (apple, mountain, bicycle). Prevents the brain from forming anxious narratives.

items.title: Gratitude List
items.description: Name 3 things you're grateful for from today. Shifts focus from worries to positives.

items.title: Tomorrow's Plan
items.description: Write tomorrow's to-do list before bed. Externalizing plans reduces 'remembering' anxiety.

items.title: Paradoxical Intention
items.description: Try to stay awake with eyes open in the dark. Reducing effort to sleep often allows sleep to come.

items.title: Melatonin Timing
items.description: If using melatonin, take 0.5-3mg 30-60 minutes before bed. Lower doses are often more effective.

items.title: Magnesium Glycinate
items.description: Consider 200-400mg magnesium glycinate before bed. Well-absorbed form that supports relaxation.

items.title: L-Theanine
items.description: 100-200mg L-theanine promotes calm without drowsiness. Found naturally in tea.

items.title: Valerian Root
items.description: Herbal supplement used for centuries. May take 2-4 weeks for full effect.

items.title: Passionflower Tea
items.description: Mild sedative effect, especially helpful for anxiety-related sleep issues.

items.title: Blue Light Glasses
items.description: Wear blue light blocking glasses 2-3 hours before bed when using screens.

items.title: Night Mode Settings
items.description: Enable night/warm mode on all devices. Schedule to activate automatically at sunset.

items.title: Sleep Tracking App
items.description: Use apps like Sleep Cycle or AutoSleep to understand patterns. Track without obsessing.

items.title: Smart Alarm
items.description: Use alarms that wake you during light sleep phases. Less jarring than traditional alarms.

items.title: Sunset Lamp
items.description: Use a lamp that simulates sunset, gradually dimming and warming over 30-60 minutes.

items.title: Pain Management Before Bed
items.description: Address pain proactively - heating pad, gentle stretches, medications on schedule.

items.title: Elevation for Breathing
items.description: Use pillows or adjustable bed to elevate upper body if breathing issues affect sleep.

items.title: Temperature Regulation
items.description: Layer blankets for easy adjustment. Keep water nearby. Some conditions cause temperature swings.

items.title: Bathroom Proximity
items.description: Keep path to bathroom clear and lightly lit. Night lights along the route.

items.title: Medication Timing Review
items.description: Work with doctor to optimize medication timing. Some meds are better at different times.

items.title: Pacing During Day
items.description: Avoid boom-bust cycles. Consistent activity levels lead to more consistent sleep.

items.title: Rest vs Sleep
items.description: Accept that rest has value even without sleep. Quiet, dark time still helps recovery.

items.title: CPAP Comfort
items.description: If using CPAP, optimize mask fit and humidity. Discomfort reduces compliance.

items.title: Symptom Log
items.description: Track symptoms and sleep quality to identify patterns. Data helps conversations with doctors.

items.title: Gentle Position Changes
items.description: Use body pillows for support. Change positions to prevent stiffness without fully waking.

items.title: Anxiety Wind-Down Protocol
items.description: 30 min before bed: journal worries, do breathing exercises, then pleasant visualization.

items.title: Depression Morning Light
items.description: Use a 10,000 lux light box for 20-30 min each morning. Helps regulate mood and sleep.

items.title: Nightmare Rehearsal
items.description: Rewrite recurring nightmares with positive endings while awake. Rehearse new version before sleep.

items.title: Safety Object
items.description: Keep a comforting object nearby - stuffed animal, partner's item, weighted blanket.

items.title: Crisis Plan Review
items.description: Have a written plan for nighttime distress. Knowing what to do reduces panic.

items.title: 20-Minute Rule
items.description: If not asleep in 20 minutes, get up. Do something boring in dim light until sleepy.

items.title: Sleep Restriction
items.description: Temporarily limit time in bed to actual sleep time. Builds sleep pressure. Use with guidance.

items.title: Stimulus Control
items.description: Only use bed for sleep and intimacy. Rebuild the bed-sleep association.

items.title: Clock Hiding
items.description: Turn clocks away from view. Clock-watching increases anxiety and vigilance.

items.title: Boring Audio
items.description: Listen to extremely boring content - academic lectures, financial reports. Occupies mind without engaging.

items.title: Different Schedules Talk
items.description: Discuss mismatched sleep schedules openly. Find compromises that work for both.

items.title: Separate Blankets
items.description: Use individual blankets to prevent cover-stealing and temperature preference issues.

items.title: Snoring Solutions
items.description: Address snoring with nose strips, elevated pillows, or sleep study referral if severe.

items.title: Movement Mattress
items.description: Consider memory foam or split mattress to reduce partner movement transfer.

items.title: Pre-Sleep Connection
items.description: Brief check-in or cuddle before turning away to sleep. Maintains connection.

items.title: Blackout for Day Sleep
items.description: Create complete darkness for daytime sleep with blackout curtains and eye mask.

items.title: Strategic Caffeine
items.description: Use caffeine strategically for shift work but avoid within 6 hours of sleep time.

items.title: Light Exposure Timing
items.description: Use bright light at start of shift, avoid before sleep. Sunglasses when leaving morning shift.

items.title: Anchor Sleep
items.description: Keep at least 4 hours of sleep at the same time daily, even on days off.

items.title: Family Communication
items.description: Educate family about sleep needs. Use do-not-disturb signs and silent phones.

items.title: Jet Lag Prevention
items.description: Start shifting sleep schedule 3 days before travel. 1 hour per day toward destination time.

items.title: Travel Sleep Kit
items.description: Pack eye mask, earplugs, familiar pillow case, and sleep tea bags for consistency away from home.

items.title: Destination Time Immediately
items.description: Switch to destination time as soon as you board the plane. Eat and sleep on new schedule.

items.title: Hotel Room Prep
items.description: Check room for light leaks, noise, and temperature. Request room changes if needed.

items.title: Avoid Arrival Naps
items.description: Stay awake until local bedtime if arriving during day. Helps reset faster.

items.title: Winter Light Therapy
items.description: Use light therapy lamp in dark winter mornings. 10,000 lux for 20-30 minutes.

items.title: Summer Sleep Cooling
items.description: Use cooling sheets, fan, or AC to combat summer heat that disrupts sleep.

items.title: Daylight Saving Adjustment
items.description: Shift sleep time by 15 minutes per day for 4 days before time change.

items.title: Allergy Management
items.description: During allergy season, shower before bed and keep windows closed. Use air purifier.

items.title: Holiday Sleep Protection
items.description: Maintain sleep schedule during holidays as much as possible. Brief variations are okay.
